goodwill_characteristics.nature: Intangible asset arising from business combination
goodwill_characteristics.not_amortized: Goodwill is NOT amortized (exception: private company may elect amortization)
goodwill_characteristics.tested_for_impairment: At least annually, or more frequently if triggering events occur
goodwill_characteristics.unit_of_account: Reporting unit (operating segment or one level below)

impairment_testing_approach.timing: At least annually, and whenever events/circumstances indicate possible impairment

qualitative_assessment_step_0.purpose: Determine whether quantitative test is necessary
qualitative_assessment_step_0.question: Is it more likely than not (>50%) that FV of reporting unit < carrying amount?
qualitative_assessment_step_0.if_no: No further testing required - no impairment
factors_to_consider: Sustained decrease in share price (for public companies)
Impairment of assets within reporting unit
qualitative_assessment_step_0.benefit: May skip costly quantitative test if clearly no impairment

quantitative_test_step_1.process: Compare FV of reporting unit to its carrying amount (including goodwill)
comparison: If FV ≥ Carrying amount → No impairment
If FV < Carrying amount → Impairment = Carrying amount - FV
quantitative_test_step_1.impairment_loss: Limited to carrying amount of goodwill allocated to reporting unit (cannot write down below zero)
quantitative_test_step_1.recognition: Recognize impairment loss in income (operating expense)
quantitative_test_step_1.reversal: Goodwill impairment losses CANNOT be reversed

analysis: Step 1: Compare FV to carrying amount
Limited to goodwill balance ($200,000), so full $100,000 recognized
calculation_example.journal_entry:
DR Impairment Loss - Goodwill $100,000
   CR Goodwill $100,000

examples_requiring_interim_testing: Significant adverse change in business climate
Unanticipated competition or loss of key personnel
Impairment of significant asset group within reporting unit
Loss of major customer or contract
Significant decline in stock price (for public companies)

options: Amortize goodwill on straight-line basis over 10 years (or less if shorter useful life)
Perform impairment testing at entity level (instead of reporting unit level)

rows: At asset or asset group level

reporting_unit_determination.definition: Operating segment or one level below (component)
component_is_reporting_unit_if: Constitutes a business or could be considered a business
Segment management regularly reviews operating results
reporting_unit_determination.aggregation: Components with similar economic characteristics may be aggregated

goodwill_allocation.principle: Allocate goodwill to reporting units that benefit from acquisition synergies
goodwill_allocation.method: Based on relative fair values of reporting units at acquisition date
goodwill_allocation.note: Once allocated, goodwill remains with reporting unit (unless disposed)

cpa_exam_strategies.testing_sequence: Optional qualitative first. If more likely than not impaired (>50%), do quantitative.
cpa_exam_strategies.quantitative_test: Simple comparison: FV < Carrying amount? If yes, impairment = difference (limited to goodwill balance).
cpa_exam_strategies.key_difference: Goodwill: One-step test (FV vs CA). Long-lived assets: Two-step (recoverability, then FV).
cpa_exam_strategies.no_reversal: Goodwill impairment NEVER reversed (unlike some other assets under IFRS).
cpa_exam_strategies.annual_requirement: Goodwill tested at least annually (long-lived assets only when indicators present).

key_points: Goodwill NOT amortized, tested for impairment annually + when triggering events occur
Optional qualitative assessment: Skip quantitative if >50% likely FV ≥ Carrying amount
Quantitative test: FV of reporting unit < Carrying amount = Impairment
Impairment loss = Carrying amount - FV (limited to goodwill balance)
Recognize impairment in income, CANNOT reverse
Private companies may elect to amortize over 10 years
Testing at reporting unit level (not individual asset level)
